original_question: Do all monomial ideals in the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n, 0) lie in the closure of the curvilinear locus?
target_in_paper: Section 2.7, (Solved) Problem XXX: "Do all monomial ideals in Hilb_d(A^n,0) lie in the closure of the curvilinear locus?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's exact target almost verbatim: it asks about monomial ideals in the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n,0) and whether they belong to the closure of the curvilinear locus. This is precisely the official formulation of (Solved) Problem XXX in Section 2.7.
missing_details: The paper works over an algebraically closed field k.
The ambient affine space should be understood as A^n_k, with coordinate ring k[x_1,...,x_n].
The quantifiers are implicit in the paper: the question is for arbitrary integers n,d >= 1.
Here d means the degree/length of the finite subscheme, equivalently dim_k(k[x_1,...,x_n]/I) = d.
Hilb_d(A^n_k,0) means the punctual Hilbert scheme, i.e. the fiber of the Hilbert-Chow morphism over d·0; its k-points are precisely the length-d subschemes supported only at the origin.

A "monomial ideal in Hilb_d(A^n_k,0)" should be read as a monomial ideal I subset k[x_1,...,x_n] of colength d whose support is {0}, so that [Spec(k[x_1,...,x_n]/I)] is a point of the punctual Hilbert scheme.
The curvilinear locus in the punctual Hilbert scheme is the locus of points [Z] such that Z is abstractly isomorphic to Spec k[t]/(t^d).
The relevant closure is the Zariski closure inside Hilb_d(A^n_k,0).
No further hypotheses such as Gorenstein, complete intersection, or characteristic-zero assumptions are part of this particular problem.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field. For every n,d >= 1, does every monomial ideal I subset k[x_1,...,x_n] with dim_k(k[x_1,...,x_n]/I) = d and support equal to {0} define a point of the Zariski closure of the curvilinear locus in the punctual Hilbert scheme Hilb_d(A^n_k,0), where the curvilinear locus consists of those length-d subschemes Z supported at 0 that are abstractly isomorphic to Spec k[t]/(t^d)?
justification: The draft matches exactly Section 2.7, (Solved) Problem XXX. To make it fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, one has to import the standing conventions from Section 1.3: the base field k is algebraically closed, Hilb_d(A^n_k,0) denotes the punctual Hilbert scheme of length-d subschemes supported at 0, and d denotes degree/length. One also has to import the earlier definition from Section 2.1 that the curvilinear locus in the punctual Hilbert scheme is the locus of subschemes abstractly isomorphic to Spec k[t]/(t^d). The sentence immediately after Problem XXX shows that the intended scope is specifically curvilinearity inside the punctual Hilbert scheme, not the broader smoothability question in the full Hilbert scheme. The paper additionally notes that this problem was solved during review, citing [11].
